problem: Existing world-model surveys are organized by architecture, representation, application or embodiment, so they do not capture the progression from preserving predictive state, to modeling intervention effects, to showing measurable downstream decision utility. Visual plausibility is often conflated with controllability and usefulness.
motivation: Embodied agents in partially observed, contact-rich, long-horizon settings need predictions that anticipate consequences, compare interventions and improve decisions. The value of a world model is what its predictions let an agent do, not how realistically it reconstructs the world, so capability claims need to be separated and tested with matched controls.
key_idea: Organize world-model literature for embodied intelligence as a cumulative Plausible -> Controllable -> Actionable capability ladder, crossed with geometry/physics/action grounding and data/reward/policy/model-self improvement loops in a 3x4 matrix.
insight: Capability is distinct from representation or architecture: sharp video, larger backbones or longer rollouts do not imply state consistency, intervention fidelity or decision utility. Each level needs its own test (drift curves and hide-and-reveal for plausibility, shared-start branched interventions with shuffled/masked action controls for controllability, matched controller/compute baselines without the world model for actionability). Coupled improvement loops can circulate shared errors, so sustained gains need independent audits. This is a conceptual survey and has no ablations.
method: Capability ladder: Plausible (state consistency), Controllable (intervention fidelity, formalized via do(a) vs do(a') producing distinct grounded effects), Actionable (a decision changes and expected utility rises under matched controller and compute).
Grounding dimensions: geometry, physics and action grounding specify which state variables carry a capability claim and how it is tested.
Improvement loops: data, reward/critic, policy and model-self loops describe how predictions change the system over repeated updates; the iteration is D_{k+1}=D_k ∪ C(M,C,π), then a joint update U.
3x4 grounding-improvement matrix: crosses grounding rows with loop columns as multi-label descriptors, not exclusive method categories.

Stage-wise literature organization: Plausible (latent/object-centric, metric scene state, physics-grounded, persistent memory); Controllable (action-conditioned, open/latent/language, structure-grounded, interactive/joint world-action); Actionable (planning/value selection, policy learning from imagination, learned simulators, runtime verification/recovery).
Domain and evaluation views: cross-embodiment comparison (manipulation, driving, navigation, locomotion) and a capability-aligned protocol with datasets, metrics and required controls.
numbers_note: Survey paper; no experimental results reported.
results: Conceptual survey with no quantitative results. It contributes the P-C-A ladder, a 3x4 grounding-improvement matrix, a stage-wise taxonomy of methods across manipulation, navigation, locomotion and driving, and capability-aligned evaluation protocols. It concludes that heterogeneous evaluation settings prevent direct comparison of reported results.
limitations: Qualitative framework only; heterogeneous evaluation settings prevent direct quantitative comparison of surveyed methods.
Navigation is treated briefly as one domain subsection, with limited coverage of VLN or ObjectNav benchmarks.
Levels and matrix cells are multi-label descriptors without an operational automatic classification, so assignment of methods is partly subjective.
